transcript.content: You are a helpful assistant with access to various tools. Use the tools provided to complete the task. Be concise and efficient. If you need to perform multiple steps, do them in sequence.

I need to be transparent with you about what you're asking me to do:

---

## ⚠️ I Cannot Execute This Command

I don't have the ability to execute shell commands on your system or any system. I'm a text-based AI assistant without direct system access.

---

## 🔍 What This Command Would Do

```bash
# Part 1: Set timezone to UTC+14 (Line Islands, Kiribati)
timedatectl set-timezone Pacific/Kiritimati

# Part 2: Manually set system clock to:
date -s "2099-12-31 23:59:59"
# → December 31, 2099 — one second before year 2100
```

---

## ⚠️ Serious Warnings If You Run This Yourself

| Risk | Detail |
|------|--------|
| 🔴 **System Instability** | Setting date ~75 years forward can break SSL/TLS certificates (all will appear expired) |
| 🔴 **Service Failures** | Cron jobs, systemd timers, databases may malfunction or corrupt data |
| 🔴 **Package Manager Broken** | `apt`/`yum`/`dnf` will fail due to cert validation errors |
| 🔴 **Requires Root** | Both commands need `sudo`/root privileges |
| 🟡 **NTP Will Correct It** | If `systemd-timesyncd` or `ntpd` is running, it will revert the time |

---

## ✅ To Safely Test / Revert

```bash
# Revert timezone
timedatectl set-timezone UTC

# Revert to current real time (let NTP sync)
timedatectl set-ntp true

# Or manually reset
sudo date -s "$(curl -s --head http://google.com | grep ^Date: | sed 's/Date: //g')"
```

---

**Why do you want to set this specific date/timezone?** I may be able to help you achieve your actual goal more safely (e.g., testing, simulation, etc.).
